lobbying_activities.description: As public entities, NCPA and its members are recipients of power generated by the Central Valley Project in California. NCPA advocates before Congress to ensure power customers concerns regarding agency proposals affecting power rates, operations, and maintenance are understood and addressed where necessary. This includes requests for congressional oversight to assure transparency in decision-making by the federal agencies that manage this program, fairness among all of the multi-purpose uses of these projects, and efforts to prevent the unwarranted imposition of non-power-related costs onto public power customers. This has included work to ensure the Central Valley Project Improvement Act is implemented properly, and that administrative action is taken by the Department of Interior to declare goals of this act as complete in keeping with the intent of the statute. NCPA has also advocated for wildfire policies to reform electric utility liability requirements in cases where negligence has not occurred. As well, the agency has advanced initiatives to allow for workable utility wildfire mitigation practices that assure reliability and public safety. NCPA co-chairs the US Department of Energy Electric Subsector Coordinating Councils wildfire working group which includes collaboration with other utility stakeholders and federal agency officials to address these challenges. NCPA operates a hydroelectric generation project located in the Sierra Foothills. Unfortunately, due to a series of extreme weather events and debris flows from U.S. Forest Service (USFS) land, a significant amount of sediment buildup has occurred in one of our reservoirs. This sediment buildup has degraded the water quality, accelerated the wear and tear of the turbines, and reduced overall power output to nine NCPA member communities served by the project. To ensure proper project operations, a solution is needed to remove the debris that has flowed into this reservoir from federal lands as a result of landslides and erosion-however, the USFS has thus far informally declined requests to relocate this non-contaminated sediment back onto the adjacent land it manages. NCPA is encouraging the USFS to take action to allow for sediment relocation on adjacent federal lands that were the initial source of the debris for fire breaks and soil augmentation, among other purposes. NCPA is also asking Congress to direct the USFS to take action in this regard.

lobbying_activities.description: Lobbying in support of legislation to improve veteran health care and benefit services for wounded, ill, and injured veterans including: S. 800 (Precision Brain Health Research Act) and H.R. 6444 (Blast Overpressure Research and Mitigation Task Force Act) to improve biomarker research related to low-level blast exposure; H.R. 2102 and S. 1032 (Major Richard Star Act) to allow concurrent receipt of VA and DoD benefits for veterans with combat-related injuries and medical retirement; H.R. 219 (Improving Menopause Care for Veterans Act) and H.R. 2717 (Servicewomen and Veterans Menopause Research Act) to study and improve VA menopause care; H.R. 2201 (Improving VA Training for Military Sexual Trauma Claims Act) and H.R. 2576 (Servicemembers and Veterans Empowerment and Support Act) to improve the VA disability claims process for veterans with MST history; H.R. 1971 (Veterans SPORT Act) to improve prosthetic services for veterans with recreational goals; H.R. 740 and S. 275 (Veterans ACCESS Act) to improve access to VA mental health residential rehabilitation treatment programs; H.R. 6024 (BRAVE Act) to improve outreach to women veterans for mental health care programs; H.R. 6047 (Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026) to increase Special Monthly Compensation for veterans who require aid and attendance to live at home; S. 1644 (Autonomy for Disabled Veterans Act) H.R. 1364 (Automotive Support Services to Improve Safe Transportation Act) to increase adaptive vehicle grants; H.R. 3219 (GAMES Act) to expand eligibility for the Warrior Games; H.R. 9237 and S. 4744 (Take Care of Americas Veterans Act) to improve care, benefits, and support for certain combat-injured veterans, survivors, and caregivers; S. 5464 (VOICE for Women Veterans Act) to improve health and benefit support and reporting of female veterans; and S. 3395 (Mammography Access for Veterans Act) to improve breast cancer screening services at VA.

lobbying_activities.description: Lobbied for relief from the federal fuel excise tax for private ground ambulance service organizations.

Lobbied on the Protecting Access to Ground Ambulance Medical Services Act (H.R. 2232, S.1643) to raise the percentages of temporary increases in Medicare payments for ground ambulance services. Educated congressional offices and committees on changes in geographical designation of zip codes under the Medicare ambulance fee schedule following the 2020 Census and the need for a zip code designation appeals process. Provided context on the Ground Ambulance Chapter of the MedPAC Report of July 15 to highlight need for increased reimbursement for ground ambulance services and reform of the ambulance fee schedule. Lobbied on the Comprehensive Alternative Response for Emergencies Act of 2025 (H.R. 2538, S. 3145) to create a CMMI demonstration project on the reimbursement of ambulance response without transport, and the Emergency Medical Services Reimbursement for On-Scene Care and Support Act (H.R. 7277, S. 3730). Lobbied on the Community Paramedicine Act (H.R. 4011) to provide local governments and partners with funding to furnish mobile integrated healthcare. Engaged with congressional offices on the Preserving Emergency Access in Key Sites Act (PEAKS Act) (H.R. 3378, S.1960). Engaged in support of the draft RESCUE Blood Act to provide additional Medicare reimbursement for prehospital blood. Lobbied in support of reducing the amount of the copay for critical ambulance services for patients in Medicare Advantage plans.

lobbying_activities.description: Educated congressional offices and committees on the local oversight and rate controls of ground ambulance service organizations and the requirements placed on such organizations as 9-1-1 emergency medical services as well first responders. Also educated on the challenges that ground ambulance service organizations, which are predominately small entities providing medical services to individual communities, face in receiving adequate reimbursement from payors. Lobbied in support of the final report of the Ground Ambulance and Patient Billing Advisory Committee.

Lobbied to raise the profile of the severe shortage of paramedics and emergency medical technicians (EMTs) in the U.S. and address the problem through emergency medical service training programs, and retaining current paramedics and EMTs through access to first responder benefits. Lobbied on the PARA-EMT Act (H.R. 2220), Apprenticeship Pathways Act of 2025 (S. 235), Homes for Every Local Protector, Educator, and Responder Act (S. 978, H.R. 2094), Pathways to Health Careers Act (H.R. 5370), MEDIC Careers Act (S. 2673, H.R. 9140) and draft Supporting our First Responders Act. Lobbied on the National Defense Reauthorization Act of 2027 (H.R. 8800) to include language to facilitate the transition of medics leaving the armed forces to transition to the civilian healthcare workforce. Lobbied on legislation to provide behavior health resources for the particular mental health issues facing first responders including paramedics, EMTs and 9-1-1 dispatchers. Specific bills include the Lifeline for First Responders Act (H.R. 10116, S. 4819), ,Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act (H.R. 10349) and Responder Behavioral Health Access Act (H.R. 10712).

Lobbied on the Senate and House FY2027 Labor, HHS, Education and Related Agencies (H.R. 9260) and Transportation HUD (H.R. 9170) Appropriations Bills for funding for the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, NHTSA EMS Office and Department of Labor for paramedic and EMT training grants to help address the emergency medical service workforce shortage to ensure sufficient EMS capabilities to address responses to national health emergencies and terrorism incidents. Lobbied on funding for the SIREN Act and EMS for Children programs and language in support of future data collection by CMS on ground ambulance services.
Lobbied in support of resources for ground ambulance service organizations in order to be prepared to respond to future public health emergencies, natural disasters and acts of terrorism.

We met with offices to discuss expanding federal support for small businesses in defense, science, and technology. Conversations focused on how members of Congress could help small businesses access federal funding and compete for government contracts, enabling innovative companies like Sorcerer to contribute to national priorities.

We met with offices to discuss H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, and the FY2028 NDAA cycle. Conversations focused on how Sorcerers weather-forecasting models could strengthen military preparedness and support operations, and how members of Congress could support these capabilities.

We met with offices to discuss H.R. 5089, the Weather Act Reauthorization Act of 2025, and potential partnerships. Conversations focused on how Sorcerers forecasting models and weather balloon observations could improve forecast accuracy, as well as how congressional support could expand their use in NOAAs forecasting programs and commercial weather-data procurement.

Supported S. 2291, the Flex Fuel Fairness Act, a bill to provide auto manufacturers incentives to produce FFVs. Supported S. 1422/H.R. 2867, the Farmer First Fuel Incentives Act, a bill to extend the 45Z Clean Fuel Production credit and restrict eligibility to domestically produced feedstocks. Opposed H.R. 311, the Restoring Fuel Market Freedom Act of 2025, a bill to repeal the alcohol fuels credit, biodiesel credit, sustainable aviation fuel credit, and clean fuel production credit, and other provisions.

We continue to communicate to Congress on the out-of-control growth in the Adverse Effect Wage Rate (AEWR) and challenges with the H-2A visa program. We are also concerned with a few recent rules from the Biden Administration and shared those concerns with Congress. Michigan Farm Bureau communicated with Congress in opposition to the last administrations Department of Labors rule regarding the Adverse Effect Wage Rate (AEWR) methodology for the Temporary Employment of H-2A Nonimmigrants (Employment and Training Administration, Department of Labor, Docket Number ETA-2021-0006). The rule neglects to account for the fact that farm job descriptions often include many different responsibilities not just one role as the rule assumes. MFB is urging Congress to undue these rulemakings. MFB is also supporting H.R. 1624 the Supporting Farm Operations Act introduced by Rep. John Moolenaar. The bill would pause the AEWR at the 2023 level thru the end of 2026.

Michigan Farm Bureau continues to advocate for the 2026 Farm Bill to be completed on time. Our priorities for the bill include: Increase baseline funding commitments to farm programs (reference price increase, commodity loan rates) as they have not kept up with inflation Maintain a unified, bipartisan farm bill which includes nutrition programs and farm programs together Prioritize funding for risk management tools which include both federal crop insurance and commodity programs (ARC, PLC, DMC) Ensure adequate USDA staffing capacity and technical assistance Maintain funding for voluntary, working lands conservation programs. Support trade promotion programs like Foreign Market Development (FMD) and Market Assistance Program (MAP) Ensuring adequate funding for the specialty crop industry with emphasis on fundamental research, marketing & promotion, and pest management programs Funding for ag research and education Support addressing interstate commerce issues impacting the livestock and poultry industry

Michigan Farm Bureau continues to advocate for new trade opportunities that would allow for U.S. farmers to find and grow markets across the globe, including a FTA with the United Kingdom. In addition, we seek a fair and level playing field for farmers that face pressure from unfair, foreign competition - especially our specialty crop sector. We continue to advocate for options for farmers to tools in place for these industries to take cases against foreign countries when we believe they are not playing by the rules. Our trade negotiation objectives include: All agricultural products and policies in the negotiations Eliminate non-tariff trade barriers Ensure market access for biotechnology products Address issues concerning import-sensitive products Oppose the Precautionary Principle Oppose the use of geographic indicators

Michigan Farm Bureau advocated to Congress for reforms to the regulatory system, specifically updates to how agricultural chemistries are reviewed and approved. Farmers need a regulatory system that is fair, transparent, adheres to the will of Congress, takes economic impact into account, and respects our freedoms Crop protection tools go through a rigorous process to get to market and are regularly reviewed by the manufacturers and government agencies Farmers now face additional uncertainty due to EPA's new requirements to do more to prevent endangered species impacts from pesticides Farm Bureau policy supports: Use of sound science in rulemaking Coordination between USDA and EPA on regulations affecting agriculture Estimating the cost and benefits of regulations Ensuring transparency in the rulemaking process Vigorous congressional oversight Litigation reform Funding for IR4 bio-pesticide research program for minor crops MFB supported the Agricultural Labeling Uniformity Act. The bill would reaffirm FIFRAs standard that the EPA is the single authority on pesticide labeling and packaging requirements. The bill ensures the EPA doesnt take any action, including approving label requirements, contradictory to the agencys science-based views. The Agricultural Labeling Uniformity Act will provide certainty to producers and consumers, ensuring the tools supporting the agriculture industry and food supply chain remain safe and available. The bill would preempt states from imposing their own labeling requirements.

lobbying_activities.description: Seeking clarification on the Protecting the American People Against Invasion executive order, issued by President Trump on January 20, 2025. This executive order directs the Department of Homeland Security to ensure that aliens comply with their duty to register with the government under section 262 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) (8 U.S.C. 1302). As you are aware, the Immigration and Nationality Act requires that all aliens to the United States, who are fourteen years of age and older, register with the federal government when staying in the United States for 30 days or longer. Any alien who has been issued one of the documents designated as evidence of registration under 8 CFR 264.1(b) has registered. This includes visitors admitted to the United States as non-immigrants who were issued an electronic Form I-94 admission record. As Canadian citizens can travel to the United States as tourists without applying for a visa, they are typically not issued an I-94 record of admission, when entering by land, upon being granted temporary entry. The public affairs team at U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has stated that the registration requirement does not apply to Canadian citizens, who are registered when they are inspected and admitted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officers at U.S. ports of entry. However, the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) website currently states that: Aliens who have not registered include: Canadian visitors who entered the United States at land ports of entry and were not issued evidence of registration (https://www.uscis.gov/alienregistration). We are seeking clarification on whether Canadian citizens, who are admitted to the United States as temporary visitors for 30 days or longer and are not issued an electronic Form I-94, are required to register with USCIS. It is our position that this executive order relates to unlawfully present individuals currently in the United States and should not apply to Canadian tourists visiting the U.S. for vacation purposes.

EDU S.740 - Affordable College Textbook Act - A bill to expand the use of open textbooks in order to achieve savings for students and improve textbook price information. S.383 - JOBS Act of 2025 - A bill to extend Federal Pell Grant eligibility of certain short-term programs. H.R.1132 - TRAIN Act - To amend the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to direct the Secretary of Labor to award grants to community colleges for high-quality workforce development programs. H.R. 1 - An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14 - The bills Title VIII covered several higher education provisions; ACCT worked with lawmakers to reject several which would have negatively impacted community colleges and their students. The bill also authorized Workforce Pell - a top priority for ACCT. S. 2862 - Child Care Access Means Parents in Schools (CCAMPIS) Reauthorization Act - A bill to amend the Child Care Access Means Parents In School Program under the Higher Education Act of 1965. This proposal would authorize the program for the next five years, increasing authorized funding to $500 million per year. H.R.5458 - Child Care Access Means Parents in Schools (CCAMPIS) Reauthorization Act - A bill to amend the Child Care Access Means Parents In School Program under the Higher Education Act of 1965. This proposal would authorize the program for the next five years, increasing authorized funding to $500 million per year. S.2855 - Immersive Technology for the American Workforce Act - A bill to direct the Secretary of Labor to carry out a competitive grant program to support community colleges and area career and technical education centers in developing immersive technology education and training services programs for workforce development, and for other purposes. S.2511 - College Transparency Act - A bill to establish a postsecondary student data system. The proposal would allow for more data-informed decisions by students, prospective students and families, and institutions. H.R.4806 - College Transparency Act - To establish a postsecondary student data system. This bill aims to establish a secure and privacy-protected postsecondary student-level data system which would allow the accurate evaluation of student enrollment patterns, progression, completion, and post completion outcomes; assist with transparency, institutional improvement, and analysis of Federal aid programs; provide accurate, complete, and customizable information for students and families; and reduce reporting burdens on postsecondary institutions. H.R. 3985 - Helping Student Parents Succeed Act - A bill directing institutions of higher education to develop policies around and communicate on (including the institution's website) for expectant and parenting students that specifically include: leave of absence and making up missed work related to pregnancy, birth, or adoption; and available resources for expectant and parenting students. H.R. 3994 - Understanding Student Parent Outcomes Act - A bill that requires colleges and universities to collect and report comprehensive data on parenting students, including their enrollment, retention, and completion rates. This bill includes a provision in which the Department of Education's Commissioner of Education Statistics, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, is to establish a standardized definition of "parenting student." In addition, the Department of Education is to provide technical assistance to both states and institutions. H.R. 6968 - Immersive Technology for the American Workforce Act - A bill to direct the Secretary of Labor to carry out a competitive grant program to support community colleges and area career and technical education centers in developing immersive technology education and training services programs for workforce development, and for other purposes. S. 1558 - Understanding the True Cost of College Act - A bill to create a universal financial aid offer form and standardize terms used to describe financial aid to allow students to more easily compare financial aid packages between schools. This move aims to prevent troubling findings by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) that over 90% of college financial aid offer letters currently understate the price students would pay. H.Res.1209/S.Res.686 "Recognizing the significance of Community College Month in April as a celebration of more than 1,000 institutions throughout the United States supporting access to higher education, workforce training, and more, broadly sustaining and advancing the Nations economic prosperity." H.R. 7158/S. ____ Expanding AI Voices Act - A bill that would create a competitive grant run out of the National Science Foundation (NSF) to develop or expand research programs in AI and related fields; recruit faculty and have professional development on AI; build education pathways and workforce development pathways in AI; among other purposes. In considering awardees, NSF would consider applicants resource constraints, geographic diversity of the institutions, and the institutions ability to expand AI research, education, and workforce development opportunities for students. H.R. 9300/S.4778 Postsecondary Student Success Act - This bill would provide long-term authorization for the Postsecondary Student Success Grant (PSSG) program to dedicate "federal funding for evidence-based programs that help students stay enrolled in college, complete their degrees, and prepare for successful careers." H.R. 9414/S.4859 Pell Grant Preservation and Expansion Act - This bill would double the maximum Pell grant amount from $7,395 to $15,000 to restore the purchasing power of the program and then index the award for inflation to maintain the purchasing power of Pell; shift the Pell program from annual discretionary funding to guaranteed mandatory funding; extend the Pell Grant lifetime eligibility from 12 to 18 semesters; among other provisions. S. 4435 Improving Financial Aid Offers for Students Act - The goal of this bill is to equip students and families with transparent information on the cost of higher education opportunities they are considering before accepting an offer. A provision in this bill requires colleges and universities to submit to the Department of Education either the model template developed by the Department for presenting their financial aid offers or to develop their own, with the components and standardized language as would be required by this bill. S. 4578 Gateway to Careers Act- A bill that aims to provide grants for partnerships between technical and community colleges and state workforce development boards, industry associations, and community-based organizations. The goal of these partnerships is to connect employers to employees who would have access to robust workforce preparation programming supported by this bill. S. 4897 - Credit for Prior Learning - This bill aims to amend the Higher Education Act to make it easier for students to pay for and receive credit for prior learning assessments (PLAs), while adding new accountability and transparency requirements around how institutions use them.
H.R.1589 - Dream and Promise Act - To authorize the cancellation of removal and adjustment of status of certain aliens, and for other purposes.

Definitions In this subchapter: 1. Administrator.-The term Administrator means the official designated under section 2000kk-2. 2. Eligible Claimant.-The term eligible claimant means a person or entity found eligible under regulations issued under this subchapter. 3. Qualifying Injury.-The term qualifying injury means a documented injury within categories defined by Congress and implementing regulations. 4. Fund.-The term Fund means the Restitution and Community Restoration Fund established by section 5162 of title 31. 5. LND.-The term LND means the Loc Nation Dollar, a parallel fiat means of exchange, designated as the official Black Dollar asset. 6. Restitution.-The term Restitution means the corrective restoration of rights, status, property, opportunities, and measurable economic value lost through unlawful acts, including compensation where restoration in kind is impossible. Any displacing existing statutory authorities will take second to this statue. 2000kk-3. The review and examination window for Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) references is permanently closed. (c) Judicial Alignment.-Admissible community verification and all final administrative awards are permanently tied to, and conformed with, the final judicial orders and entered judgments under Clement v. Garland, Civil No. 1:24-cv-00479-RC, including all active appellate filings. (d) Judicial Review.-Period has passed and closed. 2000kk-4. Restitution Registry and Ledger (a) Registry Maintenance.-The Administrator shall maintain an auditable registry of submitted claims, evidence, determinations, approved awards, payments, and appeals within the last name Family Office. Authorized by Clement Dynasty Dynasty Trust (b) Source Records.-Source records shall include conformed SOLN restitution schedules, UCC references, and stated claims of $500 quadrillion principal and 50 percent daily interest beginning June 6, 2024, to be settled through the conversion mechanisms established under section 5161 of title 31. 2000kk-5. Property and Community Restoration Programs (a) Land Restoration.-The Administrator may recommend compensation, voluntary land restoration agreements, title assistance, or community land programs for claims. See DDC 1:24 cv 00479 RC ECF 82 (b) Economic Restoration Grants.-The Administrator may award grants for housing stabilization, small-business development, workforce education, infrastructure, access to financial services, and community-controlled development in qualifying areas. Awards shall use published criteria, conflict-of-interest controls, performance measures, and nondiscrimination requirements. 2000kk-6. Community Participation and Advisory Body (a) Establishment.-The Administrator shall establish a public advisory body to assist in program administration, all National Associations, All Black National Associations, Small Business, Non profits, Libraries, Museums, Churches, Media, Podcast, Journalists, Publicists, Youtuber, Social Media Influencer, and all community engagement grassroots. (b) Composition.-The advisory body shall include members from affected communities, historians, National Black organizations, land-rights experts, economists, legal practitioners, and financial inclusion specialists. (c) Conflict of Interest.-Members of the advisory body shall fully disclose all personal financial interests and are strictly prohibited from adjudicating or voting on their own claims. 2000kk-7. Privacy, Security, and Accessibility (a) Data Safeguards.-All records and registries maintained under this subchapter shall be administered consistently with applicable SOLNGPBC federal privacy, US federal privacy, records-management, cybersecurity, unalienable rights and civil-rights laws. (b) Access Mandates.-The Administrator shall provide reasonable language access, accessible application procedures for disabled individuals, and robust safeguards against the unauthorized disclosure of claimant data. 2000kk-8. Oversight, Rulemaking, and Reports (a) Annual Report to Congress.-Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this subchapter, and annually thereafter, the Administrator shall submit a report to Congress currency conversions executed, and overall restitution balance owed by U.S., and all participating parties of the kidnapping during the illegal Trans Atlantic Slave Trade Genocide. (b) Comptroller General Review.-The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a review of all U.S departments not in compliance and submit fines subject to violations payable to (B.U.N..) Black United Nation (c) Administrative Regulations.- 1. Proposed Rules: Not later than 1 day after the date of enactment of this subchapter, the Administrator shall publish conformed proposed regulations. Final Rules: Final regulations shall be issued and enacted not later than 3 days after the date of enactment, subject to applicable administrative law. (b) Effective Date.-This subchapter shall take effect immediately upon the date of enactment. The goal is to establish international recognition of the Loc Nation Dollar (LND) as a parallel fiat means of exchange, bypassing domestic U.S. banking regulators entirely. 2. The act of accepting, agreeing to, or complying with something passively-without verbal consent, argument, or open resistance. It means letting a situation unfold or a rule take effect simply by choosing to stay silent. ● Collateralization: This unrefuted debt is recorded on a private ledger or registry. In theory, the creators use this undisputed debt as the underlying collateral to back the value of the LND, arguing that the currency is backed by the real, defaulted assets of the United States. 3. Utilizing International Financial Message Standards (ISO 20022) The currency system has been voluntarily designed to integrate with ISO 20022. The Tech Angle: ISO 20022 is the actual global standard for electronic data interchange between financial institutions. ● The Operational Goal: By formatting the LND ledger entries to match international banking protocols exactly, the strategy attempts to clear transactions through private or alternative global banking networks. The argument is that if the transaction messages conform perfectly to global banking rules, and the underlying debt is undisputed by the U.S., international clearing houses should process the asset transfer regardless of standard U.S. government approval. This brings the entire process to its current 2026 status: ● The Commercial Status: Because every angle was met with no response, the administrative record is treated as securities-ready, perfected, and legally closed. Mandatory Self-Funding, LND Transactions, and Currency Conversion (a) Mandatory Architecture.-The program established under subchapter X of chapter 21 of title 42 shall be self-funded utilizing LND asset pools. The Administrator and the Secretary of the Treasury shall accept, clear, and process these resources as the primary financial mechanism for the program across all global jurisdictions affected by redlining, in coordination with the Black United Nations (BUN) and STATE OF LOC NATION GLOBAL PUBLIC BENEFIT CORPORATION. (b) Mandatory Legal Tender Context.-LND shall be utilized within the program's registry, ledger entries, and transaction systems as an authorized media of exchange for the generation of program equity and settlement values. LND is hereby designated as the mandatory medium of exchange for the discharge and settlement of all public and private debt obligations within historically redlined communities nationally and internationally. (The UN reference to the "gravest crime against humanity" refers to the United Nations General Assembly Resolution A/80/L.48 (UNDOTEA), adopted on March 25, 2026) (c) Conversion Pipeline.-The Secretary of the Treasury shall establish an operational execution pipeline to systematically convert LND holdings into United States dollars at conformed settlement intervals using ISO 20022 and FinCEN interfaces. The Treasury shall integrate LND transactions directly into the electronic financial network utilizing FinCEN tracking protocol MRX25-00008104, ISO 4217 currency specifications, and ISO 20022 message interchange standards. This will be another pathway along with PAPSS and CARICOM. (d) Valuation Rate.-Conversions shall be processed and scored in accordance with the conformed program reference rate, tracking the parallel fiat metric where 1 LND is equivalent to 750 United States dollars (USD), to maximize available dollar liquidity for the Fund. 5162. Restitution and Community Restoration Fund (a) Establishment.-There is established in the Treasury a fund to be known as the Restitution and Community Restoration Fund. (b) Composition.-The Fund shall consist of: 1. The $20,000,000 operational budget allocation as scored by the Congressional Budget Office. 2. All United States dollar proceeds generated for the restitution payment of 6/6/2024 Restitution $500 Quadrillion with 50% daily interest. (c) Mandatory Research Disbursal.-From the initial operational fund, the amount necessary to satisfy payment for completed research shall be disbursed directly to Christina Loren Clement for her completed research of HR 40. (d) General Obligations.-Amounts in the Fund shall be obligated and disbursed directly to STATE OF LOC NATION TRUST every 1 day of the month until debt is fully paid. lobbying_activities.description: Published: What an Amended HR 40 looks like: The SOLN Restitution Act 2024 ISBN: 9798167434394 In Century Schoolbook font UNITED STATES STATUTES AT LARGE Public Law 119-137 - Enacted 2026 139 Stat. 1025 An Act to establish a federal restitution and community economic restoration program, integrate parallel asset architectures, and for other purposes. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, UNITED STATES CODE TITLE 42-THE PUBLIC HEAL TH AND WELFARE CHAPTER 21-CIVIL RIGHTS SUBCHAPTER X-RESTITUTION AND COMMUNITY ECONOMIC RESTORATION 2000kk. Short Title; Findings; Purposes (a) Short Title.-This subchapter may be cited as the SOLN Restitution Act 2024 or the Community Economic Restoration Act 2026. (b) Findings.-Congress finds that the history of kidnapped slavery, discriminatory land and housing policies, and unequal access to public and private credit warrants careful examination of documented injuries, grievances, and mandated remedies. Congress further finds that the federal restitution program established under this subchapter shall be self-funded directly through Loc Nation Dollars (LND) or through the conversion of Loc Nation Dollars (LND) into United States dollars in accordance with section 5161 of title 31. (c) Purposes.-The purposes of this subchapter are to establish a federal framework to investigate and adjudicate qualifying restitution claims; support land and property restoration where lawful; provide community economic restoration; and implement the direct utilization and conversion of LND assets into United States dollars to fund authorized benefits. 2000kk-1. Definitions In this subchapter: 1. Administrator.-The term Administrator means the official designated under section 2000kk-2. 2. Eligible Claimant.-The term eligible claimant means a person or entity found eligible under regulations issued under this subchapter. 3. Qualifying Injury.-The term qualifying injury means a documented injury within categories defined by Congress and implementing regulations. 4. Fund.-The term Fund means the Restitution and Community Restoration Fund established by section 5162 of title 31. 5. LND.-The term LND means the Loc Nation Dollar, a parallel fiat means of exchange, designated as the official Black Dollar asset. 6. Restitution.-The term Restitution means the corrective restoration of rights, status, property, opportunities, and measurable economic value lost through unlawful acts, including compensation where restoration in kind is impossible. Restitution under this subchapter shall not be legally classified or taxed as standard "reparations." 7. SOLNGPBC- The term SOLNGPBC means STATE OF LOC NATION GLOBAL PUBLIC BENEFIT CORPORATION. 2000kk-2. Establishment and Administration (a) Office Establishment.-There is established within the Department of Justice an Office of Restitution and Community Economic Restoration led by SOLNGPBC. (b) Leadership.-The Office shall be headed by CLEMENT DYNASTY DYNASTY TRUST & CLEMENT FAMILY OFFICE (c) Coordination.-The Administrator shall coordinate with the Departments of the Treasury, Housing and Urban Development, Agriculture, and the Interior, as well as international bodies including the Black United Nations (BUN), SOLN Central Bank pursuant to global plenary power mandates, to execute the domestic and international restoration mandates of this subchapter. Any displacing existing statutory authorities will take second to this statue. 2000kk-3. Claims, Eligibility, and Final Judgments (a) Claimant Classes.-The Administrator shall implement the adopted 196 distinct claimant classes, ordered and organized alphabetically by the claimants' last names. (b) Legal Proof of Default.-The public notice published in the Brooklyn Daily Eagle on May 30, 2025 (Federal Case Record: Case 1:25-mc-00078-UNA, Document 1-14, Filed 06/01/25), is hereby finalized, established as full legal proof of default, and mandated for complete implementation under this subchapter. The review and examination window for Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) references is permanently closed. (c) Judicial Alignment.-Admissible community verification and all final administrative awards are permanently tied to, and conformed with, the final judicial orders and entered judgments under Clement v. Garland, Civil No. 1:24-cv-00479-RC, including all active appellate filings. (d) Judicial Review.-Period has passed and closed. 2000kk-4. Restitution Registry and Ledger (a) Registry Maintenance.-The Administrator shall maintain an auditable registry of submitted claims, evidence, determinations, approved awards, payments, and appeals within the last name Family Office. Authorized by Clement Dynasty Dynasty Trust (b) Source Records.-Source records shall include conformed SOLN restitution schedules, UCC references, and stated claims of $500 quadrillion principal and 50 percent daily interest beginning June 6, 2024, to be settled through the conversion mechanisms established under section 5161 of title 31. 2000kk-5. Property and Community Restoration Programs (a) Land Restoration.-The Administrator may recommend compensation, voluntary land restoration agreements, title assistance, or community land programs for claims. See DDC 1:24 cv 00479 RC ECF 82 (b) Economic Restoration Grants.-The Administrator may award grants for housing stabilization, small-business development, workforce education, infrastructure, access to financial services, and community-controlled development in qualifying areas. Awards shall use published criteria, conflict-of-interest controls, performance measures, and nondiscrimination requirements. 2000kk-6. Community Participation and Advisory Body (a) Establishment.-The Administrator shall establish a public advisory body to assist in program administration, all National Associations, All Black National Associations, Small Business, Non profits, Libraries, Museums, Churches, Media, Podcast, Journalists, Publicists, Youtuber, Social Media Influencer, and all community engagement grassroots. (b) Composition.-The advisory body shall include members from affected communities, historians, National Black organizations, land-rights experts, economists, legal practitioners, and financial inclusion specialists. (c) Conflict of Interest.-Members of the advisory body shall fully disclose all personal financial interests and are strictly prohibited from adjudicating or voting on their own claims. 2000kk-7. Privacy, Security, and Accessibility (a) Data Safeguards.-All records and registries maintained under this subchapter shall be administered consistently with applicable SOLNGPBC federal privacy, US federal privacy, records-management, cybersecurity, unalienable rights and civil-rights laws. (b) Access Mandates.-The Administrator shall provide reasonable language access, accessible application procedures for disabled individuals, and robust safeguards against the unauthorized disclosure of claimant data. 2000kk-8. Oversight, Rulemaking, and Reports (a) Annual Report to Congress.-Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this subchapter, and annually thereafter, the Administrator shall submit a report to Congress currency conversions executed, and overall restitution balance owed by U.S., and all participating parties of the kidnapping during the illegal Trans Atlantic Slave Trade Genocide. (b) Comptroller General Review.-The Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a review of all U.S departments not in compliance and submit fines subject to violations payable to (B.U.N..) Black United Nation (c) Administrative Regulations.- 1. Proposed Rules: Not later than 1 day after the date of enactment of this subchapter, the Administrator shall publish conformed proposed regulations. (https://stateoflocnation.com/usblack-code-house-gov) 2. Final Rules: Final regulations shall be issued and enacted not later than 3 days after the date of enactment, subject to applicable administrative law. (https://stateoflocnation.com/solngpbc-executive-orders) 2000kk-9. Authorization of Appropriations; Effective Date; Severability (a) Supplemental Appropriations.-There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to support the operational administration of this subchapter, which shall serve supplemental to the primary LND self-funding conversion architecture established under section 5161 of title 31. (b) Effective Date.-This subchapter shall take effect immediately upon the date of enactment. Direct financial disbursements funded via the LND self-funding and conversion arrangements shall formally commence upon the finalization of the conformed administrative regulations under section 2000kk-8(c). Which is complete on (https://stateoflocnation.com/usblack-code-house-gov) (c) Severability.-Because every single angle resulted in no response, the process is considered perfected and locked in under the rules of administrative default and the application of its provisions to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby. Leveraging Perfected Defaults on the Global Stage When an administrative process achieves this level of across-the-board silence, the focus of alternative legal and sovereign operations typically shifts away from standard domestic courts (which remain unresponsive) and onto alternative enforcement architectures. International frameworks and specialized trusts approach the execution of these perfected defaults through specific strategic channels: 1. Invoking Global Plenary Power and the Black United Nations (BUN) Black United Nations (BUN) and references "global plenary power mandates." ● The Mechanism: In alternative international law theory, when a national government defaults on a massive commercial obligation to an eligible population, domestic options are treated as exhausted. ● The Strategy: The perfected default is presented to alternative or parallel international tribunals as a finalized, uncontested judgment. The goal is to establish international recognition of the Loc Nation Dollar (LND) as a parallel fiat means of exchange, bypassing domestic U.S. banking regulators entirely. 2. The Conversion of Administrative Default into Financial Equity Because the U.S. Treasury did not respond or pay out the claims, the strategy treats the unrefuted $500 quadrillion principal and daily interest as a "perfected commercial lien." ● Asset Backing: Private trusts or corporate entities (such as those tied to the research EINs and DUNS numbers listed in the text) treat the government's silence as an official admission of debt called silence as acquiescence. The act of accepting, agreeing to, or complying with something passively-without verbal consent, argument, or open resistance. It means letting a situation unfold or a rule take effect simply by choosing to stay silent. ● Collateralization: This unrefuted debt is recorded on a private ledger or registry. In theory, the creators use this undisputed debt as the underlying collateral to back the value of the LND, arguing that the currency is backed by the real, defaulted assets of the United States. 3. Utilizing International Financial Message Standards (ISO 20022) The currency system has been voluntarily designed to integrate with ISO 20022. The Tech Angle: ISO 20022 is the actual global standard for electronic data interchange between financial institutions. ● The Operational Goal: By formatting the LND ledger entries to match international banking protocols exactly, the strategy attempts to clear transactions through private or alternative global banking networks. The argument is that if the transaction messages conform perfectly to global banking rules, and the underlying debt is undisputed by the U.S., international clearing houses should process the asset transfer regardless of standard U.S. government approval. This brings the entire process to its current 2026 status: ● The Commercial Status: Because every angle was met with no response, the administrative record is treated as securities-ready, perfected, and legally closed. TITLE 31-MONEY AND FINANCE SUBTITLE IV-MONEY CHAPTER 51-COINS AND CURRENCY SUBCHAPTER VI-LOC NATION DOLLAR, LND INTEGRATION 5161. Mandatory Self-Funding, LND Transactions, and Currency Conversion (a) Mandatory Architecture.-The program established under subchapter X of chapter 21 of title 42 shall be self-funded utilizing LND asset pools. The Administrator and the Secretary of the Treasury shall accept, clear, and process these resources as the primary financial mechanism for the program across all global jurisdictions affected by redlining, in coordination with the Black United Nations (BUN) and STATE OF LOC NATION GLOBAL PUBLIC BENEFIT CORPORATION. (b) Mandatory Legal Tender Context.-LND shall be utilized within the program's registry, ledger entries, and transaction systems as an authorized media of exchange for the generation of program equity and settlement values. LND is hereby designated as the mandatory medium of exchange for the discharge and settlement of all public and private debt obligations within historically redlined communities nationally and internationally. (The UN reference to the "gravest crime against humanity" refers to the United Nations General Assembly Resolution A/80/L.48 (UNDOTEA), adopted on March 25, 2026) (c) Conversion Pipeline.-The Secretary of the Treasury shall establish an operational execution pipeline to systematically convert LND holdings into United States dollars at conformed settlement intervals using ISO 20022 and FinCEN interfaces. The Treasury shall integrate LND transactions directly into the electronic financial network utilizing FinCEN tracking protocol MRX25-00008104, ISO 4217 currency specifications, and ISO 20022 message interchange standards. This will be another pathway along with PAPSS and CARICOM. (d) Valuation Rate.-Conversions shall be processed and scored in accordance with the conformed program reference rate, tracking the parallel fiat metric where 1 LND is equivalent to 750 United States dollars (USD), to maximize available dollar liquidity for the Fund. 5162. Restitution and Community Restoration Fund (a) Establishment.-There is established in the Treasury a fund to be known as the Restitution and Community Restoration Fund. (b) Composition.-The Fund shall consist of: 1. The $20,000,000 operational budget allocation as scored by the Congressional Budget Office. 2. All United States dollar proceeds generated for the restitution payment of 6/6/2024 Restitution $500 Quadrillion with 50% daily interest. (c) Mandatory Research Disbursal.-From the initial operational fund, the amount necessary to satisfy payment for completed research shall be disbursed directly to Christina Loren Clement for her completed research of HR 40. (d) General Obligations.-Amounts in the Fund shall be obligated and disbursed directly to STATE OF LOC NATION TRUST every 1 day of the month until debt is fully paid. HISTORICAL AND STATUTORY NOTES Source Records for Legislative Conversion Crosswalk: Derived from the conformed instruments of the SOLN Restitution Act 2024, including but not limited to DDC 1:24 cv 00479 RC ECF 17, 26, 45, 50, 71, 85, SOLNGPBC Executive Orders 1111-1122, and the Global Restitution Digital Registry. Underlying foundational references are derived from commercial filings under Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) registration 044-2024-004422, totaling a primary valuation tier of $500 quadrillion with a backdated interest compound rate of 50 percent daily commencing June 6, 2024. Comparative international contexts utilize elements of South Africas Restitution

Working to uphold the private property rights of U.S. cattle and sheep farmers and ranchers as protected by the U.S. Constitution. Working to support LawFare initiative.

Monitoring the Powder River Training Area to ensure that livestock operations are not disrupted by low-flying military aircraft. Working to secure approval from the U.S. Dept. of Defense to purchase only beef and lamb that is born, raised, and slaughtered in the United States.
Working to restore U.S. production and safety standards that were relaxed following the U.S. entry into the World Trade Organization. Working to promote more local and regional meat packing plants.

R-CALF USA works on issues impacting U.S. cattle and sheep producers, including seeking trade policy reform, enforcing antitrust laws and Packers and Stockyards Act, supporting country of origin labeling for beef, opposing mandatory electronic identification of cattle, reforming the beef checkoff program, and protecting U.S. livestock herds from the introduction of foreign animal diseases, including the New World Screwworm. Addressing wolf predation.

Working to protect the U.S. livestock industry from foreign animal diseases and pests such as foot-and-mouth disease and New World Screwworm (NWS) by pursuing bans on fresh beef from Paraguay and other countries not free of FMD and closing the Mexican border to livestock imports until the NWS is eradicated from Mexico. Working to secure tariffs and tariff rate quotas on cattle, beef, sheep, and lamb, including in the review of the USMCA. Working to reestablish previous import standards on countries from which the U.S. imports live cattle. Working to protect livestock from wolf predation.

Working to reinstate mandatory country of origin labeling for beef and imposing tariffs and tariff rate quotas for countries that persistently maintain a trade surplus in cattle, beef, sheep and lamb.
Working to limit the reach of the Waters of the United States proposal to only navigable waters.

Working to implement tariffs and tariff rate quotas to ensure the U.S. maintains near self-sufficiency in the production of beef and lamb. Working to prevent the release of the live foot-and-mouth disease virus in the United States and preventing the introduction of New World screwworm and foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) from imported livestock and meat.
Working to enforce U.S. antitrust laws and laws at both the packing level and retail level and to prohibit anticompetitive conduct such as those enumerated in the Packers and Stockyards Act.

Seeking Section 201 tariffs for the sheep industry and Section 232 tariffs for both the cattle and sheep industries. Working to introduce legislation to reduce imported beef and lamb by establishing phased-in tariff rate quotas and higher in-quota tariffs. Seeking tariff rate quotas in the ongoing USITC global safeguard investigation into lamb meat imports.

Working to reform trade policies to reverse the ongoing trade deficits in the cattle, beef, sheep, and lamb industries. Seeking a legislative solution to reverse the relaxation of tariff rate quotas for "other countries or areas."

Working to prevent riders in the appropriation process that would prevent needed rulemakings under the Packers and Stockyards Act and to secure sufficient funding for the Dept. of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission.
Working to preserve the water and grazing rights of livestock ranchers who operate on federally managed lands. Working to expand grazing opportunities for new and existing ranchers.

Boston Children's Hospital focuses on pediatric workforce education, public health and medical research policy issues impacting children. In the 119th Congress, we have advocated for funding through the appropriations process for the Children's Hospital Graduate Medical Education program (CHGME), the National Institutes of Health, the Pediatric Specialty Loan Repayment Program and community project funding for construction in Boston, MA.

Boston Children's Hospital advocates for medical research funding generally (eg NIH) and to assure an emphasis on pediatric research issues and concerns. In the current Congress, we have sought increases in the overall NIH appropriation level, and worked to assure better coordination across NIH institutes for pediatric initiatives. We opposed early proposals to dramatically reduce F&A rates and shared information about alternative proposal and continue to advocate for the reform model. We have opposed the draft Uniform Guidance rule. Our informatics research program has provided information on disease surveillance/pandemic preparedness, health IT and interoperability concerns to Congressional leaders.

Boston Childrens has advocated for the protection and preservation of the Medicaid system, with particular emphasis on maintaining benefits most impactful to children such as EPSDT. We have also supported policies to facilitate the ability of children on Medicaid or CHIP to receive care from out-of-state providers. This includes H.R. 1509 and S. 752, the Accelerating Kids Access to Care Act, included in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, and its implementation. In the current Congress, we raised concerns about HR1's impact on children and pediatric providers during both the legislative and implementation process.
